comment: Section 4.3.1 gives data structures priority over actors and workflows. Stable minimum data models are essential, especially for authoritative registries, but data created through operational transactions also depends on who performs the work, at which workflow step, and for what purpose. The SMART Guidelines example in section 4.3.2 presents personas, workflows, data elements and decision logic together rather than as a data-only sequence.

public.text: Section 4.3.1 gives data structures priority over actors and workflows. Stable minimum data models are essential, especially for authoritative registries, but data created through operational transactions also depends on who performs the work, at which workflow step, and for what purpose. The SMART Guidelines example in section 4.3.2 presents personas, workflows, data elements and decision logic together rather than as a data-only sequence.
public.suggestedRevision: Retitle section 4.3.1 as 'Design Data Models with Defined Actors and Workflows'. State that, where data is created through an operational transaction, the minimum data model should be designed and validated alongside the actors, workflow steps and decision logic that produce and use it. The sections may remain separate, but should be presented as a coordinated specification activity rather than a strict data-first sequence.
